questions.q: A mirror in the first quadrant is in the shape of a hyperbola whose equation is $\mathrm{xy}=1.$ A light source in the second quadrant emits a beam of light that hits the mirror at the point $(2,1 / 2)$. If the reflected ray is parallel to the $\mathrm{y}$-axis the slope of the incident beam is
questions.solution: Slope of tangent at $\left(2, \frac{1}{2}\right) $\begin{array}{l}$\mathrm{m}=$-$\frac{1}{4}$\\ $\tan \theta=-\frac{1}{\mathrm{y}}\\ \theta=\phi-90^{{}^{\circ}} \\ $\tan \theta=4$ \end{array}$ Slope of $incident ray=\mathrm{m}$\begin{array}{l}$\left|\frac{m-\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)$}{1+m $\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)$}\right|=$\tan \theta=4$ \\ $\left|\frac{4 m+1}{4-m}\right|$=4 \\ 4 m+1=16-4 m \\ m=$\frac{15}{8} \end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: On a rectangular hyperbola $x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2}, a > 0,$ three points $A, B, C$ are taken as follows $: A = \left(- a, 0\right); B$ and $C$ are placed symmetrically with respect to the $X$-axis on the branch of the hyperbola not containing $A$. Suppose that the $\Delta ABC$ is equilateral. If the side length of the $\Delta ABC$ is $ka,$ then $k$ lies in the interval
questions.solution:
We have rectangular hyperbola

$x^{2} - y^{2} = a^{2}$

Given $ABC$ is an equilateral triangle.

$∴AB = BC = AC$

$AB^{2} = BC^{2}$

$a^{2}\left(sec\theta + 1\right){}^{2} + a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta = 4a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \left(sec\theta + 1\right){}^{2} = 3\tan^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \left(sec\theta +1\right){}^{2} = 3 \left(\sec^{2}\theta -$1\right)$

$⇒ $\left(sec\theta +1\right)${}^{2} = 3 \lleft(sec\theta +1\\right)\lleft(sec\theta -1\right)$

$⇒ sec\theta +1 = 3sec\theta -3$

$⇒ sec\theta =2$

$⇒ \theta =60 °$

$∵$ Side $BC = 2atan\theta$

$= 2atan60 ° = $2a\sqrt{3}$

But side of triangle is $ka$.

$∴ka = $2a\sqrt{3}$

$k = $2\sqrt{3}$

Hence, $k \in (2,4]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Suppose $a, b$ are real numbers such that $a b \neq 0.$ Which of the following four figures represents the curve $(\mathrm{y}-a \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{b})\left(\mathrm{bx}^{2}+\mathrm{ay}^{2}-\mathrm{ab}\right)=0 ?$
questions.solution:
$\quad y=a x+b$ and $\frac{x^{2}}{a}+\frac{y^{2}}{b}=1$
slope $=\mathrm{a}$
for the line, $y$ intercept $=b$
Fig. 1 for line $\rightarrow \mathrm{a} < 0, \mathrm{ b} > 0$ hence the other fig. cannot be an ellipse Fig.2 $\quad \mathrm{a} > 0, \mathrm{ b} < 0$ hence the fig. is a hyperbola
Similarly you can check rest 2 options

questions.q: The sound of a cannon firing is heard one second later at a position $\mathrm{B}$ than at position $\mathrm{A}.$ If the speed of sound is uniform, then
options: The positions $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are foci of a hyperbola, with cannon's position on one branch of the hyperbola
the position $A$ and $B$ are foci of an ellipse with cannon's position on the ellipse
One of the positions $A, B$ is focus of a parabola with cannon's position on the parabola
It is not possible to describe the positions of $A, B$ and the cannon with the given information
questions.solution: $\mathrm{PB}-\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{Vt}+\mathrm{v}-\mathrm{vt}\mathrm{PB}-\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{V}$ (const) locus of P is Hyperbola A \& B are foci of Hyperbola
